newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Hasan made Astra chief.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Hasan made Astra chief.

text.p: Shareholders of Indonesia's largest car maker PT Astra International elected on Wednesday business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan as president of the company's board of commissioners.
The shareholders at an extraordinary general meeting approved a new nine-member board of commissioners, which included former chief commissioner Abdul Rachman Ramly as vice-president.
Hasan, who made his fortune in the timber industry, heads the Nusamba group which as of February 3 had an 8.83 percent holding in Astra, making it the third largest shareholder.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto.

The group recently bought a stake in the huge Busang gold find in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province and in PT Freeport Indonesia, which runs one of the world's biggest copper and gold mines in Irian Jaya province.

The other six Astra commissioners elected on Wednesday were Anthony Salim of the conglomerate Salim Group, Usman Admadjaja of Danamon International, tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna, timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu, Torstein Stephansen and Benjamin Arman Suriadjaja.
Hasan, a close associate of President Suharto, is also a president commissioner of Bank Umum Nasional, private banks Bank Bukopin and Bank Duta and paper maker PT Kiani Kertas.
He is also a commissioner of insurance company PT Tugu Pratama Indonesia.
